results.detail: Checked against the DTSX. There is one connection manager [psql] (Data Source=psql; Initial Catalog=ALTSHULER_MSCRM) and no DTS:Configuration, so 'אין קובץ תצורה' is correct. ServerName and OrganizationName come from gen_etlvariable (Get Organization Variables, DTSX:8322-8336). There are no OLE DB Command, Execute SQL or destination components, so all CRM writes are SDK and there is no direct DML. Links whose end date has passed (dateadd(HH,3,gen_enddate) < GETDATE() and status 2, DTSX:10053-10055) get status 4. The four operator-status rules and the two create flows exist. Problems. (1) The scopeNote says 'משמעות ערכי gen_poastatus נלקחה מהערות SQL בחבילה: 2 = valid, 4 = expired, 5 = invalid, 6 = cancelled' without saying which entity. Every one of those comments is on gen_poaaccountoperator.gen_poastatus (DTSX:10055, 11969, 13889, 15807, 17699), and none is on gen_poaoperator.gen_poastatus. That makes the gen_poaoperator meanings look attributed. Yet the same summary hedges gen_poaoperator status 2 as a hypothesis. (2) summary_he says 'פוליסות פנסיה'. Get Policies has no pension or product filter (DTSX:6125-6154); 'pension' comes only from the data-flow name. (3) 'הקישורים שלהם לחשבונות (gen_poaaccountoperator)' defines the entity as account links, but the pension flow creates the same entity for policies (gen_policy, DTSX:3911). (4) 'או לעובד שברשימה' omits that the list record must be active (gen_active = 1, DTSX:485-488), and the conditions sentence omits the no-existing-link gate (DTSX:541-553, 3629-3641). Minor, not counted: 'תחזוקה יומית' rests only on the folder name DailyProcess; no schedule is in the file.

results.id: L|Package\Update Poa Operator Cancelled by Poa Account|title
results.detail: The query is right as far as it goes (DTSX:13884-13889). It selects gen_poaoperator with gen_poastatus = 2, inner-joined to gen_poaaccountoperator, having count(all links) = count(links with status 6). The derived column CancelStatus = 6 (DTSX:13041/13052) is written through ExecuteMultiple Update in batches of 500 plus a final flush (main.cs @DTSX:14164-14224). There are two problems. (1) The text states the meaning of the VALUE WRITTEN TO gen_poaoperator.gen_poastatus, 6 = 'בוטל', as fact ('ביטול ייפוי כוח מתפעל', 'מקבל סטטוס 6 ("בוטל")'). The only file label for 6 is the SQL comment '-- cancelled', on the HAVING test of gen_poaaccountoperator.gen_poastatus = 6 (DTSX:13889). Otherwise there are only the names 'Cancelled Status' and 'Update Poa Operator Cancelled', and names are not proof. This is the same analogy for which the package already hedges gen_poaoperator status 2 ('כנראה תקף – השערה'), so the claims are internally inconsistent. (2) 'כל קישורי החשבון' is narrower than the query. The HAVING counts every gen_poaaccountoperator of the operator, and that includes the policy links created by the pension flow (gen_policy, DTSX:3911; no gen_customeraccount). Also not stated: the operator must have at least one link (inner join).

results.detail: The query is gen_poaoperator status 2, inner join to links, having count(all links) = count(case when link status != 2 then 1) with the comment '-- not valid' (DTSX:11964-11969). CancelledStatus = 6 (DTSX:11121/11132) is written through an SDK ExecuteMultiple update (DTSX:11998). Problems. (1) '"בוטל"' for gen_poaoperator status 6 is stated as fact. Here there is not even an SQL comment for 6; the only labels are the names 'Cancelled Status' and 'Update Poa Operator Cancelled'. (2) NULL semantics. A link whose gen_poastatus is NULL is not counted by '!= 2' (NULL != 2 is UNKNOWN), so such a link blocks the update. 'אינם תקפים (סטטוס שונה מ-2)' does not say this. (3) 'קישורי החשבון' includes policy links (DTSX:3911), and at least one link is required. Minor, not counted alone: '(מעורב)' assumes the earlier flows (Constraints 2-5, DTSX:18796-18799) already moved the all-4, all-5 and all-6 operators. Uniform sets of other non-2 values also reach this flow, as do sets whose earlier ExecuteMultiple item failed; item faults are ignored (DTSX:14189-14205 in the by-account flow; same pattern in each update script).
